minutes.headline: Select Board heard objections to the sewer bylaw waiver and adopted sign and liquor-insurance policies before town meeting.
minutes.summary: The finance director gave the third-quarter revenue and expenditure report. The board spent a long session with the sewer commission on Article 25, where members objected to the broad waiver language. It ratified several appointments, adopted a tailings policy, a one-day liquor license insurance requirement and an election-day sign exception, and voted recommendations on several warrant articles ahead of Saturday's town meeting.

what_happened.line: The Select Board spent a long session with the sewer commission on Article 25, a sewer bylaw amendment, and reached no resolution on the waiver language.
The sewer commission is to send the board a list of proposed changes to Article 25, including a public hearing for waivers, the next day.
The board approved a tailings policy and an insurance requirement for one-day liquor licenses, with the town as additional insured.
The board approved an election-day exception to the sign policy as amended, to be sent to the school committee for adoption.
The board recommended Articles 17, 21 and 24, and deferred Articles 22, 25, 26, 29 and 30 until town meeting.

why_it_matters: Article 25 changes the sewer bylaw, and residents heard objections that its waiver section is too broad, so the wording voters see at town meeting may differ from the warrant text.
The board has not taken positions on five warrant articles, so residents will hear its views only at town meeting itself.
The board recommended the salary administration plan wage schedule (Article 21), which sets the FY23 pay scale for covered town employees and is a cost paid mostly through taxes.
watch_next: The sewer commission's list of proposed changes to Article 25, due the day after this meeting.
Town meeting on Saturday, where Articles 22, 25, 26, 29 and 30 come up with no board recommendation.
